findings.statement: CA9 is rank 1 in the convergence ranking and is carried almost entirely by the tumour cells: RCC cells hold a transcript share of [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976], so the bulk signal is tumour-intrinsic and the purity-extrapolated log2FC stays large. It already has clinical antibody history (girentuximab), so it is a biomarker/imaging target rather than a novel one.

In Visium, the neighbours of high-CA9 spots are enriched in RCC cells (log2 enrichment [gene=CA9; type=spatial_neighborhood; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; log2_enrichment=0.381]) and, more weakly, macrophages; composition-corrected attribution puts essentially all spot expression on RCC, consistent with the single-cell result.

The AlphaFold CA9 model has a mean pLDDT of [gene=CA9; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=76.56]; its top detected cavity has a volume of [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; volume_a3=126.8] A3 with one nearby accessible lysine (K109), and the cavities recover about half of experimental ligand-contact residues. This is a descriptive monomer heuristic only and says nothing about degrons or ligase compatibility.

CD70 ranks fourth in convergence with tumour-up expression in CPTAC and TCGA that persists when extrapolated to pure tumour, and RCC cells are the largest per-cell source in the scRNA data, though Treg and other lymphocytes also express it at lower levels. It has early-phase antibody and ADC history, so it is a tumour-cell target with immune co-expression to account for.

MET transcripts are mostly tumour-cell derived, with RCC cells holding a share of [gene=MET; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.935], while only a minority of RCC cells express it and endothelium contributes a small part. MET is therefore a tumour-intrinsic but heterogeneous target.

EPAS1 (HIF-2a) is not mainly a tumour-cell transcript in this dataset: [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=81.3] percent of endothelial cells express it versus [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; pct_expressing=4.9] percent of RCC cells, and fibroblasts are also high. Bulk EPAS1 signal is therefore largely stromal, and RCC-cell dropout in 10x may understate tumour expression.

KDR is an endothelial (microenvironment) target, not a tumour-cell target: endothelium holds a transcript share of [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951], consistent with the anti-angiogenic TKI rationale.

CD74 is an immune/antigen-presenting gene: macrophages hold [gene=CD74; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Macrophage; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.436] of tumour transcripts, and cDC, B cells and pDC express it in essentially all cells. Bulk elevation reflects infiltration, not tumour-cell expression.

CXCR4 is a lymphocyte gene: CD8 T cells hold [gene=CXCR4; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=CD8_T; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.563] of transcripts (driven partly by their abundance), with CD4 T, B and pDC cells also expressing it. It is an immune-microenvironment target, not tumour-intrinsic.

COL23A1 is the top tumour-track candidate: RCC cells hold a transcript share of [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881], it has few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug, is annotated as a cell-membrane protein, replicates in TCGA and stays up at pure tumour (log2FC [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88]), has no adverse survival signal, and shows no vital-organ protein enrichment. Missing: any DepMap or functional dependency (ccRCC effect is not selective), antibody-accessible epitope confirmation (SURFY and CSPA do not support surface), and literature counted by gene symbol only.

The AlphaFold model of COL23A1 has low confidence (mean pLDDT [gene=COL23A1; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=58.91]) and only a tiny, shallow cavity, so a small-molecule route looks unlikely from this monomer; an antibody or other biologic route is the more plausible one if surface display is confirmed.

RAB42 is a second tumour-track candidate made mainly by RCC cells (transcript share [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627]), with TCGA replication and purity-robust upregulation, few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug. It is an internal protein, so it is not antibody-accessible, and it has no dependency or functional evidence.

OLFML2A is a stroma-track candidate: fibroblasts hold a transcript share of [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.647], it is up in TCGA and purity-robust, with few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug. It is a secreted/extracellular protein with notable colon expression, no adverse survival signal and no dependency data, so any target would be a fibroblast microenvironment hypothesis.

JAG2 is an endothelial stroma-track candidate (Notch ligand, antibody-tractable, surface/secreted) that replicates in TCGA and is purity-robust, with no clinical drug; the effect size is modest and it has non-trivial heart expression, so endothelial specificity and off-tumour safety are unresolved.

LILRB4 is a macrophage-carried immune-track candidate (macrophage transcript share [gene=LILRB4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; source_share=0.933]) but it is flagged infiltration-driven, with log2FC at pure tumour only [gene=LILRB4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.508]. It is a tumour-associated macrophage target, not a tumour-cell one, with no ccRCC functional or dependency evidence and lung expression to assess.

MILR1 is a macrophage gene with no ccRCC papers and no clinical drug, up in TCGA and linked to adverse survival, but its signal is infiltration-driven (log2FC at pure tumour only [gene=MILR1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.414]). It could mark macrophage abundance rather than a tumour-cell vulnerability; function is untested.

NNMT ranks eighth in convergence with tumour-intrinsic, TCGA-replicated upregulation, adverse prognosis and grade association, and no clinical drug; it is a metabolic enzyme, so it is a biomarker and enzyme-target hypothesis whose ccRCC dependency has not been shown to be selective.

caveats: Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses; none has validated dependency or functional evidence, and literature is counted by gene symbol.
Single-cell transcript shares depend on how many cells of each type were captured; the RCC-cell dropout in 10x may understate EPAS1 in tumour cells.
Structural scores are a descriptive monomer heuristic; they do not identify degrons, ligase compatibility or degradation.
SC data are from 12 donors, some groups (endothelium, PT) come from few donors.
CD70 and NNMT single-cell records were not cited with numbers because no record id was available or not queried; spatial context and pockets were only run for CA9 and COL23A1.
Several top biomarkers in the convergence ranking (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD, FABP1, NPHS2, PIGR) are down in tumour and reflect lost proximal tubule identity; they were not examined at the cell level.
